chunks: And in the narration of Abī al-Ḥusayn al-Asadī, may Allah be pleased with him, that al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said:

“Indeed, the worshipper only performs a prostration after the obligatory prayer so that he may thank Allah, exalted is His mention, therein for what He has bestowed upon him of performing his obligation. And the least that suffices therein is: ‘Thanks be to Allah’ three times.”

key_terms.لِيَشْكُرَ: so that he may give thanks

ai.seo_question: What should be said in Sajdat al-Shukr after the obligatory salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the prostration after the obligatory prayer is performed as an act of gratitude to Allah for granting the servant success in fulfilling the prescribed salat (prayer). It also states the minimum sufficient dhikr in this sajdah: saying “Shukran lillah” three times.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.978 - In a narration from Abu al-Hussain al-Asadi, it is reported that Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

“Indeed, the reason a person prays a prostration of gratitude (Sajdat al-Shukr) after completing a prescribed prayer is to thank Allah (swt), the Most High, for the blessing He bestowed upon them in enabling them to perform their obligatory duty.
The least that suffices in this prostration is to say : ‘Thanks be to Allah (swt)’ (Shukran lillah) three times.”
